front-door.description: PAGE COMPOSER — assemble several standalone fragments into ONE working page (Page.vue + one file per node). Give it 1+ nodes, each `{ id, role?, scene, intent }` where scene is 'table' / 'form' / 'dialog' (at most one form; tables and dialogs may repeat) and intent is exactly that scene's standalone intent object. The wiring is derived deterministically from the artifact runtime contract: a row button whose key equals a dialog node id opens that dialog (title from the dialog intent's defaultTitle); the query form reloads the default table from page 1; reset reloads it with cleared filters; submit becomes a page event 'save'; a successful dialog submit refreshes the default table. The form fragment only emits the events its `buttons` render — `buttons` defaults to 'none' (no buttons at all: query/submit/reset never fire), 'query' emits query+reset, 'submit' emits submit+reset. Composition does NOT rewrite a node's intent, so wires from a channel that form cannot emit are reported in `warnings` (they would never fire — e.g. page 'save' with no save button). The default table is the node with role 'master', else the only table; in a multi-table page with neither, data channels become page events instead of guessing (and the artifact/envelope warnings name the upgrade and both remedies: the page's per-node `<nodeCamel>Refresh`/`<nodeCamel>Reload` methods — node `order-list` exposes `orderListRefresh`/`orderListReload` — or declare role 'master'). Pass `wires` to declare master-detail style links yourself (e.g. master row-action key 'view' → detail table reload, where the row is passed as the model; use to.model to pass only chosen row fields); an explicit wire overrides the derived one for the same source. Wire targets must be callable by the generated page: table refresh/reload, form validate/resetFields, component-dialog open/close; `open` is only reachable from a row-action (it carries the row), and a row-action key must match a declared rowButtons key. `behavior: 'ui-only'` wires only the UI (row button → dialog open) and turns query/reset/success into page events so the host performs its own requests; the default `data-wiring` only derives table reload/refresh (no HTTP requests — use scene 'crud' on `generate_scene` for built-in add/edit/delete). Use this when the user wants these pieces TOGETHER in one page but the request is not a CRUD page (use `generate_scene` with scene='crud' for a CRUD page). The page exposes refresh/reload/open and emits row-action/save (+ query/reset/success when there is no default table or behavior is ui-only). When the client supports MCP structured output, the composition envelope (nodes/wires/faces/page/fingerprint) is also returned as `structuredContent`; the text content is unchanged.

name.description: Display name for the composed page (summary only). The component name is always ComposedPage.

target.description: Page target. Defaults to the first node's explicit target, then vue3. All nodes must share one target.

behavior.description: Data-wiring mode (default 'data-wiring'). 'data-wiring' derives query/reset → default table reload and dialog onSuccess → default table refresh; it does NOT generate HTTP requests (fragment intents carry no apiUrl/actions) — use scene 'crud' for built-in add/edit/delete requests. 'ui-only' wires only the UI (row button → dialog open) and turns query/reset/success into page events so the host performs requests itself. Explicit wires apply in both modes.

id.description: Node id in kebab-case (e.g. 'users', 'query-form', 'edit'). It is the output file name (<id>.vue), the template ref source, and — for a dialog node — the row-button key that opens it ('edit' binds the 编辑 button).

role.description: Optional role label (kebab-case, unique per scene). `master` marks the table that form query/reset and dialog success default to in a multi-table page. Which row button loads a detail table is a product decision — express it in `wires`, not as a role.

scene.description: Which standalone fragment this node is. 'crud' is not composable (it is already a full page).

intent.description: The node's intent table: exactly that scene's standalone intent object (scene='table'|'form'|'dialog' — the same vocabulary the scene router takes). For a dialog, `defaultTitle` is the title used by the composed page's open().

nodes.description: The page's nodes: at most one 'form'; 'table' and 'dialog' may repeat (master-detail, multi-dialog). A row button whose key equals a dialog node id opens that dialog.

wires.description: Explicit wiring, validated against the same runtime contract as derived wiring. An explicit wire overrides the derived wire for the same source (node + channel + rowAction key). Row-action targets receive the clicked row by default (e.g. master row → detail table reload(row)); set `to.model` to pass only chosen fields (e.g. { departmentId: '$row.departmentId' }) instead of the whole row.

channel.description: Source channel declared by ARTIFACT_RUNTIME: row-action / submit / query / reset / onSuccess.

Target channel the composed page can CALL (ARTIFACT_RUNTIME.invokable): table refresh/reload, form validate/resetFields, component-dialog open/close. `model` is data, not a method. A composable dialog (mode 'composable') has no template ref — only a row-action may open it. `open` requires a row, so it is only accepted from a row-action source.

model.description: Row → reload params mapping, only for a row-action source targeting `reload`. Values are single-level row fields written as '$row.<field>' (e.g. { departmentId: '$row.departmentId' } → reload({ departmentId: row.departmentId })). Omit to pass the whole row (reload(row)).

event.description: Page event name to emit (becomes part of the page's emits face).

when.description: Required for row-action sources: the button key this wire applies to. It must match a rowButtons key declared in the source table's intent — an undeclared key would generate a branch that never fires.

contract.description: Envelope protocol version: es-plus.artifact@2 or es-plus.composition@3

fingerprint.description: Content fingerprint of the artifact / composition

full.description: COMPAT ENTRY (adapter) — same product as generate_scene with scene='crud' (byte-identical), kept for hosts that already call this name. Use it for ANY request that involves a list/table, CRUD, search + results, or multiple es-plus pieces working together. Your ONE job is to fill `surfaces`: set query/table/form field lists and the dialog list to match what the request implies (any subset is valid — table-only, query+table, table+add/edit, full CRUD, etc.). A `surfaces.dialog` entry is either a canned key ('add'/'edit'/'view') or a full object `{ key, title?, width?, fullscreen?, formItems? }` when the request names a custom dialog id/title/width or a per-dialog field list. Routing is then deterministic: table-bearing requests compile through the golden-covered single generator; no-table subsets emit self-contained fragments. Do NOT manually orchestrate generate_form/generate_table/generate_dialog for a composite page — fill surfaces here and let the routing compose them. When the user wants several standalone pieces assembled into one page (not a CRUD page), call generate_composition instead. Use the standalone tools only for an explicit single-component ask or to embed a fragment next to non-es-plus components. Optional config knobs — tableOptions / formLayout / operationColumn / tableBtns / toolbarBtns / expandConfig / treeConfig / mergeConfig — may be set alongside `surfaces`; each is forwarded verbatim into the composed config, so fill them only when the request names those specifics. A no-table request whose only surface is `dialog` emits one JSX composable PER dialog entry (named use<Key>Dialog): each entry's `formItems` overrides the shared form/query body, its `title` becomes open()'s default title, and its `width`/`fullscreen` are applied. Because the dialog body is a JSX render, that path needs a JSX plugin; if the host wants a self-contained dialog with NO JSX dependency, call generate_dialog with mode:'component' instead. When the client supports MCP structured output, the artifact envelope is also returned as `structuredContent`; the text content is unchanged.

apiUrl.description: REST base URL for this resource, e.g. "/api/users"

query.description: Filter fields shown above the table

prop.description: Field key in the data model (camelCase), e.g. "userName"

labelKey.description: i18n label key for this field (takes precedence over `label`; only takes effect once the host entry assembles the plugin with a `t` option).

formtype.description: Pick by the field's MEANING, not by keyword: status/type/enum/gender → Select; date/time → DatePicker/TimePicker; image/avatar/file → Upload; long text → Input (attrs.type:'textarea'); on/off → Switch; multi-choice → Checkbox; tree → Cascader; score → Rate; numeric value (amount/price/quantity/stock/count/money/integer) → InputNumber. Default Input.

querySpan.description: Grid width of this field in the query form (1-24; 2 columns = 12 each). Column count is set PER FIELD — there is no layout-level span key.

formSpan.description: Grid width of this field in the add/edit form (1-24; 2 columns = 12 each). Column count is set PER FIELD — there is no layout-level span key.

group.description: Form-group key for the FORM face. Fields sharing a key render inside that group's container; declare the containers in `formLayout.layout`. Ignored by table columns. Omit to follow the layout's `ungrouped` strategy.

rules.description: Validation rules for this field. Use `pattern`/`min`/`max`/`type` for format constraints and `trigger` for when validation runs; `message` is REQUIRED. A rule carrying `type` is dispatched ONLY to that type validator (async-validator `getValidationMethod`) — a `pattern` on the SAME rule is silently ignored, so when the user states BOTH a regex and a type, emit them as TWO separate rules. For a plain text length cap (e.g. '最多 20 字') prefer `attrs.maxlength`; a `min`/`max` rule validates values with a message but does not block typing. Emit these rather than dropping a format/range requirement the user stated.

required.description: Enforce a value with this rule (same effect as field-level `required`; prefer the field-level key for unconditional requirements).

pattern.description: RegExp SOURCE STRING the value must match (e.g. "^1\d{10}$"), not a RegExp object.

min.description: Minimum length for strings / minimum value for numbers.

max.description: Maximum length for strings / maximum value for numbers.

type.description: Value type validated by this rule.

message.description: Message shown when the rule fails — REQUIRED, write it in the user's language.

trigger.description: 'blur' validates when the field loses focus; 'change' validates while the value changes.

attrs.description: Extra component props, e.g. { type: 'textarea', maxlength: 200 }

dataOptions.description: Static options for Select/Radio/Checkbox/Cascader (fixed enum).

apiParams.description: Remote options source for Select/Cascader — use instead of dataOptions when options come from an API.

formatter.description: Extension point: a JS arrow-function source string for read-only cell formatting, e.g. "(row) => row.amount.toFixed(2)".

render.description: Extension point: a render-function source string for a fully custom cell/control.

isHidden.description: Conditional visibility (AI-06): PLAIN JSON data, never a JS function string. Semantics: the field is HIDDEN while the condition HOLDS (`{ field: 'payType', op: 'eq', value: 'cash' }` = hidden while payType is cash). TWO forms, never mixed within one node: (1) legacy condition `{ field, op?, value? }` — `op` is ONE of eq | ne | in | nIn | empty | notEmpty | truthy | falsy (default eq); preferred for simple comparisons; (2) JSONLogic-shaped expression node for ordering / OR / nesting, e.g. `{ '>': [{ var: 'amount' }, 100] }` or `{ or: [...] }` — expression ops (closed set): var == != > >= < <= in nin empty notEmpty truthy falsy and or not if. An expression op such as `>` or `!=` inside a legacy `{field, op, value}` node is INVALID (the runtime warns and treats the field as visible) — use form (2) for those. An ARRAY of nodes is AND (hidden only when ALL hold) and may mix both forms. Applies to the query and add/edit forms, NOT the table column.

reactions.description: Field linkage (AI-07): an array of {dependencies?, when?, fulfill} rules — PLAIN JSON, never JS callbacks. Use when THIS field's options/required/disabled/value depend on ANOTHER field (fulfill: {dataOptions?, required?, disabled?, value?}). `dependencies` lists the model paths that retrigger it (REQUIRED for fulfill.value). `when`, `fulfill.required`, `fulfill.disabled` and `fulfill.value` are JSONLogic EXPRESSION NODES only — e.g. `when: { '==': [{ var: 'country' }, 'us'] }`, `required: { '==': [{ var: 'country' }, 'us'] }` — never the `{ field, op, value }` condition form and never a bare boolean (those are for `isHidden`). `fulfill.dataOptions` is a literal option array, not an expression. One rule per case, LAST WINS. Applies to the query and add/edit forms, NOT the table column.

dependencies.description: Model paths that retrigger this rule. REQUIRED when `fulfill.value` is present.

when.description: Optional gate expression: the rule applies only while it evaluates truthy.

dataOptions.description: Literal option array for this field while the rule is active (NOT an expression — branch per case with one rule each).

required.description: Expression node evaluating to a boolean: make this field required.

disabled.description: Expression node evaluating to a boolean: disable this field.

value.description: Expression node evaluating to this field's new value, written back to the model (requires a non-empty `dependencies`).

permissionValue.description: Permission CODE gating this field (RBAC, checked by the host's global permission(code)) — NOT a data-driven condition: use `isHidden` for show/hide by another field's value, `reactions` for options/required/disabled linkage.

children.description: Nested-object FORM grouping (ONE level only): this field becomes a full-width section heading and its children render under it. Children inherit this field's `group` (their own `group` wins) and cannot declare their own `children`.

disabled.description: Expression node evaluating to a boolean: disable this field.

value.description: Expression node evaluating to this field's new value, written back to the model (requires a non-empty `dependencies`).

permissionValue.description: Permission CODE gating this field (RBAC, checked by the host's global permission(code)) — NOT a data-driven condition: use `isHidden` for show/hide by another field's value, `reactions` for options/required/disabled linkage.

fields.description: Table columns — one per column the user described

apiUrl.description: REST endpoint for the list. If set, the table auto-fetches via apiParams; if omitted, wire tableData manually.

target.description: Target renderer: vue3 (Element Plus), vue2 (Element UI), antdv (Ant Design Vue)

tableOptions.description: Container options — the SAME declarative subset as generate_crud's tableOptions (core TableOptions minus function values): appearance (border/stripe/size/showHeader/emptyText/leftText), height (heightType/tabHeight/height), columns (multiSelect/snIndex), state (cachePageSelection), row (rowkey/rowClassName/defaultSort), request (refetchKeepPage/localPagination/configTableOut), engine (virtual/engine/rowHeight/estimatedRowHeight/overscanCount), tree (treeConfig — vxe rich tree), row expand (expandConfig — vxe switch), inline edit (editConfig — requires engine:'vxe').

heightType.description: How the container height is applied: 'height' = fixed height (value from `height`, or `tabHeight` if set); 'maxHeight' = capped at `tabHeight` (a `height` value is IGNORED); 'auto' = no container height constraint. Default 'auto'.

tabHeight.description: Table height consumed for EVERY heightType: under 'height' it overrides `height`; under 'maxHeight' it is the cap. number → px, string → raw CSS value (e.g. '60vh'). Prefer it over `height` whenever a concrete height is needed — it is the only height key that applies when heightType is 'maxHeight'.

height.description: Container height used ONLY when heightType is 'height' (ignored for 'auto' / 'maxHeight' — use tabHeight there). Takes precedence over nothing: an explicit tabHeight always wins.

virtual.description: Enable virtual scrolling for large datasets. The engine is target-specific: vue3 renders the el-table-v2 engine; antdv forwards `virtual` to <a-table> (Ant Design Vue 4 has native virtual scroll); vue2 + Element UI has no equivalent and degrades to a plain el-table with a console warning — the vue2 large-data path is `engine: 'vxe'` instead. Safe to set on any target — only the rendering engine differs.

engine.description: Table rendering engine, an alternative to `virtual: true`. 'default' = the target's plain table, 'virtual' = the target's virtual engine (vue3 el-table-v2; antdv <a-table :virtual>; vue2 has no equivalent and degrades with a warning), 'vxe' = vxe-table, available on ALL THREE targets — 'vxe' is the large-data path for vue2.

rowHeight.description: Row height in px for virtual mode (vue3 / el-table-v2 only; default 50)

estimatedRowHeight.description: Estimated row height for dynamic-height virtual scrolling (vue3 / el-table-v2 only)

overscanCount.description: Buffer rows outside the visible area (vue3 / el-table-v2 only; default 2)

size.description: Table density. Default 'small' at runtime; all three targets accept these.

showHeader.description: Show the table header (default true). Set false to hide it.

emptyText.description: Text shown when there are no rows (default '暂无数据').

snIndex.description: Render a leading row-index (serial number) column.

leftText.description: Text shown on the left side of the table toolbar.

cachePageSelection.description: Persist the checkbox selection across page changes (needs a stable rowkey). Default true at runtime; set false to reset selection on page change.

refetchKeepPage.description: Keep the current page when re-fetching (default false). Query/reset still return to page 1.

localPagination.description: Paginate already-fetched data client-side instead of requesting each page from the API.

sortParam.description: Server-side sorting: every list request then carries { sortField, sortOrder } (order = 'asc' | 'desc') and a header click refetches the SAME page. { field, order } renames the two request keys. Also seeds from defaultSort. Omit to keep client-side sorting of the current page.

defaultSort.description: Default sort applied on first render.

trigger.description: How editing is entered (default 'click').

configTableOut.description: Map the LIST API response onto table semantics when the backend does not use the default flat shape. Default mapping is { total: "records", tableData: "rows", pageSize: "pageSize", current: "pageNo" }. Each value is the FLAT response key (no deep paths — the component only reads top-level keys). e.g. a backend returning { list: [...], count: N } → { tableData: "list", total: "count" }. Only the keys you set are remapped; omit a key to keep its default.

treeConfig.description: vxe-only rich tree config. Use transform:true + rowField + parentField to build a tree from FLAT rows; for nested `children` arrays on every renderer use the CRUD config's top-level `treeConfig`.

transform.description: Build the tree client-side from FLAT rows (needs rowField + parentField). vxe only.

rowField.description: Row id field for transform mode (default 'id').

parentField.description: Parent id field for transform mode (default 'parentId').

children.description: @deprecated vxe v4 alias of childrenField; normalized at runtime.

mapChildren.description: Field that caches original children in transform mode (default '_X_ROW_CHILD').

lazy.description: Lazy-load children (vxe only; the loader function itself is a Tier-3 extension point).

expandConfig.description: vxe-only row-expand switch (paired with an expand column).

accordion.description: Accordion mode: at most one row expanded at a time.

lazy.description: Lazy-load expand content (vxe only; the loader function itself is a Tier-3 extension point).

showFooter.description: Show the vxe footer row (engine:'vxe' only).

exportConfig.description: vxe export config (true = defaults); engine:'vxe' only.

toolbarConfig.description: vxe toolbar config (true = defaults); engine:'vxe' only.

columnConfig.description: vxe column config, e.g. { resizable: true, showOverflow: 'tooltip' }; engine:'vxe' only.

keepSource.description: Keep pre-edit row snapshots for revertData()/getUpdateRecords(); vxe inline editing only.

mouseConfig.description: vxe cell-selection mode ({ selected: true }); engine:'vxe' only.

seqConfig.description: vxe sequence-column startIndex (seqMethod is a function and stays out of JSON); engine:'vxe' only.

printConfig.description: vxe print config (true = defaults); engine:'vxe' only.

pagination.description: Pagination seed ({pageSize, pageSizes}); current/total are managed by the component.

pageSize.description: Rows per page on first render (runtime default 10).

pageSizes.description: Selectable page-size options shown in the pager, e.g. [10, 20, 50].

rowButtons.description: Optional operation-column buttons. Each button emits a `row-action` event (`{ key, row }`) from an inlined clickEvent and the wrapper declares `emits: ['row-action']` — the host listens on the wrapper. This is NOT the CRUD page's `triggerEvent` (that only links query/reset toolbar buttons to table refresh).

columns.description: Explicit table columns — the SAME vocabulary as generate_crud's `columns` (override, not merge): multi-level group headers via `groups`, and non-field columns via `type` (index/selection/expand). When present it REPLACES the field-derived data columns (`fields` stays required and still documents the row shape). Contract keys are sanitized exactly like the CRUD page (unknown keys dropped, `x-*` kept).

treeConfig.description: Declarative tree table — the SAME cross-renderer narrow subset as generate_crud's top-level `treeConfig` ({childrenField?, expandAll?}). Merged with tableOptions.treeConfig (this top-level key wins on conflicts). Distinct from the vxe-only `tableOptions.treeConfig`.

childrenField.description: Key name that holds a row's nested child nodes (default 'children'). Set only when the API nests children under a different key.

expandAll.description: Whether all nodes start expanded (default false).

expandConfig.description: Declarative row-expand content — the SAME shape as generate_crud's top-level `expandConfig` ({title?, fields[]}). Prepends one expand column showing a read-only field list; if `columns` already has a {type:'expand'} column, the content attaches to it. Distinct from the vxe-only `tableOptions.expandConfig`.

title.description: Optional title shown at the top of the expanded row.

prop.description: Row field to display (value = `row[prop]`).

labelKey.description: i18n label key (used with a global t() function; takes precedence over `label`).

fields.description: Read-only fields rendered inside the expanded row, one per line as `label: value`.

mergeConfig.description: Declarative row-merge ({rowsBy: ['dept','team']}) — the SAME cross-renderer narrow subset as generate_crud's top-level `mergeConfig`. Emitted as `options.mergeConfig`; el-table / a-table / vxe all honor it.

rowsBy.description: Column props to merge. Each is grouped by ADJACENT-EQUAL values: the first row of a run keeps the cell with rowspan = run length, the rest are merged away.

rowkey.description: Primary key. Same as tableOptions.rowkey; when both are set this top-level key wins (with a warning).

prop.description: Data key for this column, e.g. "userName". Omit for non-field columns (type: index/selection/expand).

label.description: Column header text. Omit for non-field columns.

labelKey.description: i18n key alternative to label (used when i18n is on)

type.description: Non-field column kind: 'index' = row number, 'selection' = checkbox column, 'expand' = row expander (needs an expandConfig/slot). Omit for a normal data column.

filters.description: Declarative column filter options (PLAIN JSON — never a JS function). Rendered by the default engines and engine:'vxe'; the virtual engine (vue3 engine:'virtual') has NO filter UI. Filtering is LOCAL (the wrapper filters rows in the browser), so do not combine it with server-side paging/proxy contracts for the same column.

text.description: Option text shown in the filter dropdown.

value.description: Row value matched by this option (loose primitive compare: 1 matches "1").

filterMultiple.description: Allow selecting several filter options at once (default true).

filterMode.description: Local comparison for `filters` (default 'equals'): 'equals' = value equality (booleans/numbers compare loosely against strings), 'includes' = the cell text CONTAINS the selected option value (text search).

autoFilters.description: Derive `filters` from this column's `dataOptions` (P2-3). When true and `filters` is omitted, each `dataOptions` entry's label/value becomes a filter option ({text, value}). Explicit `filters` always wins; no-op when dataOptions is empty or the engine is vue3 virtual (no filter UI).

permissionValue.description: Permission code; the column is not rendered without it

groups.description: Nested child columns for a GROUP HEADER (multi-level). Recursive. Cross-renderer safe up to 2 levels (antdv supports N; vue3/vue2 default tables flatten beyond 1).

editRender.description: Column-level inline editor (AI-09 子项④). vxe engine only — requires tableOptions.editConfig AND tableOptions.engine:'vxe'. Function-valued fields (events) and custom-registered renderers are out of scope (Tier-3).

name.description: Inline-edit renderer name, e.g. '$input' | '$select' | '$textarea' | '$date' (vxe engine only).

type.description: 'default' = enter edit on trigger; 'visible' = editor always shown.

options.description: Option list for a '$select' editor (label/value pairs).

props.description: Props forwarded to the editor component.

expandConfig.description: Row-expand content declared ON the `type:'expand'` column (AI-09 子项②). Same shape/semantics as the top-level `expandConfig`; use it when the expander is not the leading column or when `columns` is the source of truth. If BOTH are set, the top-level one wins on the expand column. Distinct from `tableOptions.expandConfig` (the vxe `{accordion}` switch).

title.description: Optional title shown at the top of the expanded row.

prop.description: Row field to display (value = `row[prop]`).

labelKey.description: i18n label key (used with a global t() function; takes precedence over `label`).

fields.description: Read-only fields rendered inside the expanded row, one per line as `label: value`.

front-door.description: Pre-fill a structured CRUD config from an existing schema (OpenAPI JSON, JSON Schema, a sample JSON object, a TypeScript interface/type literal, or SQL CREATE TABLE DDL). Deterministic, no LLM: it maps each property's DATA TYPE to a formtype (integer→InputNumber, boolean→Switch, string+date→DatePicker, string+enum→Select, array+enum→Checkbox, else Input). For ts-interface, JSDoc becomes the label and non-optional members become required; for sql-ddl, COMMENT becomes the label and NOT NULL/PRIMARY KEY become required. Use this as a HEAD START, then review & edit the draft (narrow the query fields, add buttons/dialogs/permissions the schema can't express) and use the draft as the reference when filling `generate_scene`'s (scene='crud') `surfaces` (map each field into query / table / form), and pass it to `validate_config` with type 'structured-crud-config' to check your edits. OpenAPI YAML is not supported in this version — convert to JSON first.

front-door.description: Apply ONE round of refinement to a pinned CRUD config. The pin is just the StructuredCrudConfig JSON you (the host) already hold — there is no server-side session. YOU apply the user's natural-language correction to produce the `revised` config, then call this tool with the `previous` (last-pinned) and `revised` JSON. It deterministically (1) validates `revised` against the authoritative schema and (2) returns a structured DIFF of what this round changed — fields added/removed, formtype/membership changes, actions, AND changed top-level blocks (dialogs / formLayout / tableOptions / buttons / columns / permissions / generation options), so a round that only adds an edit dialog or widens the form is not reported as "no change". If `revised` is invalid, you get the schema errors instead of a diff — fix and retry. When you're happy, use `revised` as the reference for filling `generate_scene`'s (scene='crud') `surfaces` — the front door composes the config and the code for you. This tool stays the validator/differ for a config you hand-author. This tool does NOT call a model; the reasoning is yours.

previous.description: JSON string of the previously pinned config (omit for the first round).

revised.description: JSON string of the config after you applied the user's correction.
